verses.text: In the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen who had been brought up with Herod the ruler, and Saul.
While they were worshipping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work I have called them to do."
So after they had fasted and prayed, they placed their hands on them and sent them off.
The Holy Spirit sent Barnabas and Saul on their way. They went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
When they arrived at Salamis, they preached God's word in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them as their helper.
They travelled through the whole island until they came to Paphos. There they met a Jewish magician, a false prophet named Bar-Jesus.
He was a friend of the governor, Sergius Paulus, who was a wise man. The governor sent for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear God's word.
But Elymas the magician, which is what his name means, tried to stop them. He tried to turn the governor away from the faith.
Then Saul, who was also called Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
and said, "You child of the devil! You are full of every kind of lie and trick, and you are an enemy of everything that is right. Will you never stop twisting the straight ways of the Lord?

Now the hand of the Lord is against you. You will be blind and will not see the light of the sun for a while." At once a dark mist came over him, and he went around looking for someone to lead him by the hand.
When the governor saw what had happened, he believed. He was amazed at the teaching about the Lord.
From Paphos, Paul and his friends sailed to Perga in Pamphylia. There John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
From Perga they went on to Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath day they went into the synagogue and sat down.
After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the leaders of the synagogue sent them a message: "Brothers, if you have a message of encouragement for the people, please speak."
Paul stood up, waved his hand, and said, "Men of Israel, and you Gentiles who worship God, listen to me.
The God of the people of Israel chose our ancestors. He made the people great while they lived as strangers in Egypt, and with his mighty power he led them out of that country.
For about forty years he put up with them in the desert.
He destroyed seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to his people as their own.
All this took about four hundred and fifty years. After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.
Then the people asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled for forty years.
After removing Saul, God made David their king. God said about him, 'I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my own heart. He will do everything I want him to do.'
From David's descendants God has brought to Israel the Saviour Jesus, as he promised.
Before Jesus came, John preached to all the people of Israel that they should turn from their sins and be baptised.
As John was finishing his work, he said, 'Who do you think I am? I am not the one you are waiting for. But someone is coming after me, and I am not good enough to untie his sandals.'
"Brothers, children of Abraham, and you Gentiles who worship God, this message of salvation has been sent to us.

The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not know who Jesus was. They did not understand the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath. But by condemning him, they made those words come true.
Even though they found no good reason to put him to death, they asked Pilate to have him killed.
When they had done everything that was written about him, they took him down from the cross and laid him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead.
For many days he was seen by those who had travelled with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to our people.
"We are telling you the good news: what God promised our ancestors
he has done for us, their children, by raising Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm, 'You are my Son. Today I have become your Father.'
God raised him from the dead, never to rot away. He said, 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.'
So he also says in another Psalm, 'You will not let your Holy One rot away.'
"David served God's purpose in his own time. Then he died, was buried with his ancestors, and his body rotted away.
But the one God raised from the dead did not rot away.
"So, brothers, I want you to know that through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is told to you.
Through him everyone who believes is set free from every sin, something the law of Moses could never do for you.
Be careful, so that what the prophets said does not happen to you:
'Look, you who mock! Wonder and die! For I am doing something in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.'"
As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people begged them to speak about these things again on the next Sabbath.
When the meeting ended, many Jews and godly people who had turned to the Jewish faith followed Paul and Barnabas. They talked with them and urged them to keep living in the grace of God.
On the next Sabbath almost the whole city came to hear the word of the Lord.
But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy. They spoke against what Paul was saying and insulted him.
Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: "We had to speak God's word to you first. But since you reject it and do not think you are worthy of eternal life, we now turn to the Gentiles.
This is what the Lord has commanded us: 'I have made you a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.'"
When the Gentiles heard this, they were glad and praised the word of the Lord. All who were chosen for eternal life believed.
The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.
But the Jews stirred up the important God-fearing women and the leading men of the city. They started an attack against Paul and Barnabas and threw them out of their area.
So Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet as a warning to them and went on to Iconium.
And the followers were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
